answer: Each agent’s influence can be weighted by a one-person credential issued after an in-person check and bound to a wallet with a zero-knowledge proof. The kernel of the scheme is that credentials are nontransferable and each can authorize only one active identity, while the proof reveals no legal name. A sybil attacker must recruit real people or repeat costly checks; minting wallets is cheap, but acquiring scarce credentials is not. velvet and zephyr can name test agents without changing that constraint.
